0.headline: InvIT IPO rush gathers pace; 4-5 private trusts likely to go public by Mar 2027
0.heading: InvIT IPO rush gathers pace; 4-5 private trusts likely to go public by Mar 2027
0.intro: Among the proposed public offerings, Brookfield-backed Altius Telecom Infrastructure Trust has filed for a potential Rs 6,000-crore IPO as it seeks to convert from a privately placed to a publicly offered InvIT.
0.body:
Four to five privately placed Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) are expected to tap the public markets by March 2027 to raise a combined Rs 17,000 crore, as infrastructure developers increasingly turn to this route to mobilise long-term capital and monetise operational assets, investment bankers said.

InvITs have already mobilised around Rs 88,000 crore through equity issuances during FY23-FY25, indicating growing investor appetite for infrastructure-backed investment opportunities, according to the Bharat InvITs Association.

Among the proposed public offerings, Brookfield-backed Altius Telecom Infrastructure Trust has filed for a potential Rs 6,000-crore IPO as it seeks to convert from a privately placed to a publicly offered InvIT.

Investcorp-backed NDR InvIT Trust is also planning to transition into a public InvIT through an issue of up to Rs 750 crore, while KKR and Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan (OTPP)-sponsored Vertis Infrastructure Trust is also exploring an IPO.

In March, NHAI-sponsored Raajmarg Infra Investment Trust raised Rs 6,000 crore through its IPO.

The growing pipeline of public offerings comes amid an expansion in India's InvIT market, estimated at around Rs 7.5 lakh crore, as infrastructure companies increasingly look at the trust structure to unlock capital from operational assets and fund future expansion.

The market is also attracting a wider pool of investors. InvITs had around 6.5 lakh unitholders as of the first quarter of FY27, and over the past 10 years, InvITs have collectively distributed nearly Rs 1 lakh crore to their investors, as per the Bharat InvITs Association.

Under SEBI regulations, InvITs are required to distribute at least 90 per cent of their net distributable cash flows to unitholders, making them an attractive investment avenue for investors seeking regular income.

The investor base is also gradually broadening, with a growing number of women participating as unitholders, according to brokers and wealth advisers.

The sector has received a further boost from the Securities and Exchange Board of India's (SEBI) introduction of a framework for depository receipts, allowing foreign investors to gain exposure to Indian REITs and InvITs through select overseas exchanges.

Several privately placed InvITs are already listed, including Interise Trust, Digital Fibre Infrastructure Trust, Anzen India Energy Yield, Sustainable Energy Infra, Intelligent Supply Chain Infrastructure, Shrem InvIT, NXT-Infra Trust, Roadstar Infra and TVS Infrastructure Trust, among others.

The expansion of the market is being supported by increasing diversification across infrastructure segments, including roads, highways, power transmission, telecom, energy and warehousing.

Roads and highways remain the largest segment, supported by asset monetisation initiatives of the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) and private infrastructure developers. Road InvITs alone account for around Rs 3 lakh crore in assets under management (AUM), representing around 44 per cent of the overall market.

Their AUM has grown at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of around 44 per cent between FY22 and FY26, highlighting the growing role of InvITs in infrastructure financing.

Power transmission has also emerged as an established segment, with trusts such as India Grid Trust and Powergrid Infrastructure Investment Trust, while Altius Telecom Infrastructure Trust represents opportunities in the telecom infrastructure space. NDR InvIT Trust, meanwhile, indicates the growing potential of warehousing and industrial parks.

However, the market performance of listed InvITs has remained mixed, with unit prices showing varying trends against their respective issue prices.

This indicates differing investor sentiment towards individual trusts and asset classes.

1.headline: Medicap Healthcare cuts IPO size by 29% to Rs 170 crore, drops pre-IPO placement
1.heading: Medicap Healthcare cuts IPO size by 29% to Rs 170 crore, drops pre-IPO placement
1.intro: Medicap Healthcare IPO | The company, which operates a manufacturing facility in Vadodara, Gujarat, specialises in manufacturing pharmaceutical closures, including Euro Head caps and bottle preforms.
1.body:
Gujarat-based pharmaceutical packaging company Medicap Healthcare has reduced the size of its initial public offering (IPO) by 29% and decided to drop the pre-IPO placement component from the revised offer structure, according to an addendum published on November 21.

In its notice to investors, the company said that, pursuant to a board resolution dated November 15, it had decided to reduce the issue size from Rs 240 crore, as disclosed in the draft red herring prospectus (DRHP), to Rs 170 crore. It also decided not to issue specified securities through a pre-IPO placement as part of the offering.

The revision is in line with SEBI regulations and related guidelines, which allow issuers to increase or decrease the fresh issue size by up to 50% without refiling the DRHP for IPOs opening on or before March 31, 2027.

Medicap Healthcare filed its draft offer document with the capital markets regulator in September 2025. Subsequently, SEBI approved the IPO papers in January 2026.

The proposed IPO initially comprised an entirely fresh issue, with no offer-for-sale (OFS) component. The fresh issue structure also included a proposed pre-IPO placement of Rs 48 crore.

The company, which operates a manufacturing facility in Vadodara, Gujarat, specialises in manufacturing pharmaceutical closures, including Euro Head caps and bottle preforms.

Following the reduction in the IPO size, Medicap Healthcare has also revised the proposed utilisation of the issue proceeds.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

Of the net proceeds, Rs 83 crore will be used to purchase plant and machinery for its existing manufacturing facility, while Rs 44 crore will be allocated towards debt repayment. The remaining proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes.

In FY26, the company manufactured approximately 45 crore units against an installed production capacity of around 80 crore units at its existing manufacturing facility.

As part of its proposed expansion, Medicap Healthcare plans to increase the facility's installed annual production capacity by 69.6 crore units for pharmaceutical packaging caps and closures and 27 crore units for bottle preforms, taking the total additional capacity to 96.6 crore units per annum.

"The proposed expansion will be undertaken by installing 29 additional injection molding machines at the existing manufacturing unit," Medicap Healthcare said in its addendum.

Meanwhile, the company had outstanding borrowings of Rs 244.9 crore on a consolidated basis and Rs 36.2 crore on a standalone basis as of November 15, 2026.

Aryaman Financial Services has been appointed as the merchant banker for the Medicap Healthcare IPO.

2.headline: Passenger mobility company Chartered Speed cuts IPO size to Rs 433 crore after SEBI regulatory changes
2.heading: Passenger mobility company Chartered Speed cuts IPO size to Rs 433 crore after SEBI regulatory changes
2.intro: Chartered Speed IPO | The revised public issue will comprise a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 333 crore and an offer-for-sale of Rs 100 crore.
2.body:
Ahmedabad-headquartered passenger mobility company Chartered Speed has reduced the size of its proposed initial public offering (IPO) to Rs 433 crore, following changes in the regulatory framework introduced by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI).

The revised IPO will comprise a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 333 crore and an offer-for-sale (OFS) of Rs 100 crore.

Under the OFS, promoters Pankaj Gandhi and his wife, Alka Gandhi, will each sell shares worth up to Rs 50 crore.

Through its regulations dated April 13 and a communication to the Association of Investment Bankers dated October 12 this year, SEBI allowed companies to increase or decrease the size of their fresh issue by up to 50 percent without refiling their draft red herring prospectus (DRHP). Chartered Speed has accordingly reduced the size of its fresh issue.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

The company had filed its draft IPO papers with the capital markets regulator in September 2025, seeking to raise Rs 855 crore. The proposed IPO comprised a fresh issue of Rs 655 crore and an OFS of Rs 200 crore. SEBI subsequently approved the company's IPO papers in January 2026.

The company has also revised the proposed utilisation of the fresh issue proceeds. Of the net proceeds, Rs 50.2 crore will be used to purchase electric buses, while Rs 205 crore will go towards debt repayment. The remaining amount will be utilised for general corporate purposes.

At the time of filing its DRHP in September 2025, Chartered Speed had an operational fleet of more than 2,000 buses as of June 2025, including 46 electric buses.

In its draft papers, the company stated that it intended to gradually phase out vehicles powered by fossil fuels, with a strong focus on sustainability. It had also set a target of converting 25 percent of its fleet into electric vehicles.

Motilal Oswal Investment Advisors and SBI Capital Markets have been appointed as the merchant bankers to manage the Chartered Speed IPO.
